newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees HK, Shanghai remaining finance centres.
newsitem.headline: China sees HK, Shanghai remaining finance centres.

text.p: China's economy is so large that it can support financial centres in both Hong Kong and Shanghai, but Shanghai would not soon replace Hong Kong, central bank vice governor Chen Yuan was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

"From a short term point of view, or at least until the renminbi becomes a completely freely convertible currency, it will not be possible for Shanghai to become an international finance centre," Chen, vice governor of the People's Bank of China, wrote in a front-page article in the Financial News.
"Of course, given the enormous scale of China's economy, it is entirely possible that it would support the development of two financial centres," he wrote.
"Shanghai and Hong Kong will develop into China's two financial centres, each with its own special characteristics, supplementing and complementing each other as financial centres," he wrote.

Officials have been trying in recent years to play down Shanghai's ambitions to recover its 1930s position as the leading city in Asia and to outstrip the booming territory of Hong Kong as China's premier international financial centre.

With the recovery of the British colony of Hong Kong just 13 days away, Beijing has been at pains to issue statements that underline China's commitment not to change Hong Kong and to nurture its status as a major financial hub.

Chen, who will attend the handover ceremony in Hong Kong at midnight on June 30, stressed the commitment of China's central bank to support the Hong Kong dollar if necessary and added that mainland Chinese financial institutions would enjoy no special treatment in Hong Kong after the handover.
